beforeClose.title: Adaptive sprint lifecycle
beforeClose.objective: Make Kyro record changing work truthfully without treating a partial sprint or exhausted roadmap as a terminal scope failure.
successCriteria: Every unfinished task has a typed, reasoned disposition before sprint closure.
Closing any sprint preserves immutable evidence while keeping the scope open for explicit next planning.
Scope completion and retirement remain explicit, distinct decisions.
Doctor and Integrity distinguish lawful lifecycle evolution from immutable-artifact corruption.
Legacy checkpoints remain readable without retroactive semantic claims.

requirements.statement: Kyro SHALL require an explicit validated disposition for every unfinished task before closing a sprint.
requirements.rationale: Unfinished work must remain discoverable and attributable instead of being represented as success or silently discarded.

requirements.statement: Kyro SHALL close a sprint without automatically completing its scope merely because all originally planned roadmap entries are closed.
requirements.rationale: A roadmap is an estimate; scope completion requires an explicit decision and evidence.

requirements.statement: Kyro SHALL allow an open scope with no active sprint to plan a subsequent sprint through the normal tool-owned flow.
requirements.rationale: Legitimate reprioritization must not require a recovery or manual state edit.

requirements.statement: Kyro SHALL preserve fail-closed validation for immutable checkpoints, unsafe paths, identity conflicts, and stale approvals while accepting lawful lifecycle evolution.
requirements.rationale: Simplification must not weaken artifact integrity or recovery safety.

requirements.statement: Kyro SHALL keep retirement distinct from scope completion and preserve readable historical checkpoint semantics.
requirements.rationale: Terminal retirement has explicit human approval semantics, and immutable historical bytes cannot be rewritten.

scenarios.given: an active sprint has unfinished tasks
scenarios.then: each unfinished task must carry a valid explicit disposition with its reason and any required continuation reference

scenarios.given: the final originally planned sprint has a mixture of completed and disposed tasks
scenarios.then: the immutable close record reports a truthful partial outcome and the scope is not automatically completed

scenarios.given: an open scope has closed all originally listed roadmap sprints
scenarios.when: the user supplies a later sprint plan
scenarios.then: kyro plan materializes it through the normal tool-owned route without recovery

scenarios.given: a scope contains either lawful lifecycle evolution or an unsafe/corrupt immutable artifact
scenarios.then: lawful evolution is distinguishable from scoped fail-closed artifact corruption

scenarios.given: a historical or retired scope is inspected
scenarios.then: historical records remain readable and retirement remains explicitly terminal and human-gated

scenarios.given: an open scope has no active sprint, no unresolved debt or review, and healthy artifacts
scenarios.when: the user explicitly confirms scope completion
scenarios.then: Kyro records completion as a distinct lifecycle fact without retiring the scope or rewriting its archive

scenarios.given: a completed but non-retired scope needs later work
scenarios.when: the user explicitly reopens it with a reason
scenarios.then: Kyro preserves completion history and routes the scope to plan_sprint without recovery or manual edits

nonGoals: Startup-contract consolidation or unrelated global preflight redesign.
NutriLens or Kyro Lens implementation changes.
Manual editing mode for Kyro-managed state.
Archive rewriting, release, installation, publication, or version bump.

conventions.rule: A post-close live-state transition is valid only if it replays exactly from the checkpoint after-image through the same builders the writer uses; lifecycle records are evidence, never authority.

roadmap.sizingRationale: The work is sequenced by semantic dependency: define the lifecycle contract first, implement the core transitions second, then reconcile integrity and certify the complete path.

sprints.title: Truthful sprint close and open-scope routing

recommendations: Before completing this scope, verify each success criterion against evidence rather than treating all-tasks-done as proof the objective was met.
If further lifecycle transitions are added (e.g. suspend/resume), extend checkpoints/lifecycle-state.ts and its replay first, then the command surface.

previousSprint.summary: Explicit scope completion and reopen replace inferred terminal states; verification replays lifecycle transitions instead of trusting records.

activeSprint.title: Integrity recalibration and lifecycle certification
activeSprint.objective: Prove that dispositions, truthful closes, explicit completion, and reopen replay identically through Doctor and Integrity without weakening immutable-artifact safety.

phases.title: Lifecycle replay parity
phases.objective: Make lifecycle replay an observable, adversarially tested contract rather than a trusted record.

tasks.title: Certify completion and reopen replay against artifacts
tasks.description: Exercise explicit completion and reopen from a closed checkpoint after-image, proving Doctor and Integrity accept only the state exactly rebuilt by the lifecycle builders and reject unexplainable drift.
tasks.context: Use the shared lifecycle builders as the sole authority. The recorded lifecycle metadata is evidence, never authority; keep legacy checkpoint reads compatible and do not rewrite archive bytes.
acceptance_criteria: Doctor and Integrity accept a completion/reopen state only when replay from the checkpoint after-image reproduces both sprint and registry state exactly.
A forged, incomplete, or extra live-state change remains a scoped DIVERGED failure with no repair or canonicalization proposal.
Historical checkpoint and retirement reads remain distinguishable from the open completion/reopen lifecycle.

evidence.summary: Made Integrity replay lifecycle records through the shared completion/reopen builders and require exact sprint plus registry reproduction; forged or extra lifecycle drift is now a scoped diverged blocker.

checked_criteria: Doctor and Integrity accept a completion/reopen state only when replay from the checkpoint after-image reproduces both sprint and registry state exactly.
A forged, incomplete, or extra live-state change remains a scoped DIVERGED failure with no repair or canonicalization proposal.
Historical checkpoint and retirement reads remain distinguishable from the open completion/reopen lifecycle.

phases.title: End-to-end adaptive lifecycle
phases.objective: Prove the ordinary developer journey needs no manual state edits or recovery detour.

tasks.title: Add an end-to-end partial-close, plan, complete, and reopen proof
tasks.description: Run the compiled CLI in an isolated workspace through disposition, truthful partial close, later sprint planning, explicit completion, and deliberate reopen, preserving checkpoints and traceability at every boundary.
tasks.context: This is the acceptance path for the original rigidity problem: unfinished work is disposed with a reason and destination, not silently completed; normal planning resumes without manual edits. Use tool-owned commands only.
acceptance_criteria: A partially completed sprint closes truthfully with typed dispositions and leaves the scope routable to plan_sprint.
The next sprint materializes through kyro plan without recovery, and explicit completion remains distinct from retirement.
A deliberate reopen preserves completion history, returns the scope to plan_sprint, and leaves every pre-existing archive byte unchanged.

evidence.summary: Added one compiled-CLI acceptance path from typed disposition through truthful partial close, follow-up planning, verified completion, and deliberate reopen; immutable archive bytes are checked across lifecycle-only steps.

checked_criteria: A partially completed sprint closes truthfully with typed dispositions and leaves the scope routable to plan_sprint.
The next sprint materializes through kyro plan without recovery, and explicit completion remains distinct from retirement.
A deliberate reopen preserves completion history, returns the scope to plan_sprint, and leaves every pre-existing archive byte unchanged.

phases.title: Objective evidence and release decision
phases.objective: Turn the scope success criteria into explicit evidence without auto-completing the scope or publishing a release.

tasks.title: Verify success criteria and certify lifecycle readiness
tasks.description: Map every scope success criterion to the completed behavioral evidence and run the full repository and scoped integrity gates; report any remaining gap as debt or a blocker instead of asserting scope completion.
tasks.context: The Sprint 2 recommendation is incorporated here: all-tasks-done is not proof of the objective. This task produces evidence for a later human scope-completion decision; it must not invoke scope complete, retirement, release, or installation.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the five scope success criteria maps to concrete passing behavior and verification evidence, or an explicit unresolved item.
npm run check, scoped Doctor, Analyze, and scoped Integrity prepare pass after the end-to-end lifecycle proof.
The resulting handoff identifies scope completion as a separate human decision rather than auto-completing the scope.

evidence.summary: Certified all five requirements: R1 typed disposition and immutable pre-close trace (T3.2 E2E); R2 truthful partial close/open scope (check-close-handoff); R3 normal follow-up plan after partial close (T3.2 E2E/check-plan); R4 exact Doctor and Integrity lifecycle replay with forged drift blocked (T3.1); R5 completion/reopen distinct from retirement and historical checkpoints readable (check-scope-retire). Scope completion remains an explicit human decision.
validation: node dist/cli.js repair integrity prepare --kyro-scope adaptive-sprint-lifecycle --json

checked_criteria: Each of the five scope success criteria maps to concrete passing behavior and verification evidence, or an explicit unresolved item.
npm run check, scoped Doctor, Analyze, and scoped Integrity prepare pass after the end-to-end lifecycle proof.
The resulting handoff identifies scope completion as a separate human decision rather than auto-completing the scope.

definitionOfDone: All Sprint 3 tasks have tool-owned evidence and a pass verdict.
The seven lifecycle scenarios replay through the compiled CLI without manual edits or archive rewrites.
Doctor, Analyze, scoped Integrity prepare, and the full repository check pass.
Each scope success criterion has explicit evidence or an honest unresolved disposition; scope completion remains a separate human decision.
